approvalSummary: Admin-only shared Next.js application on Cloudflare Workers with Supabase PostgreSQL/Auth/private Storage, separate staging and production, permanent direct-render Card routes and reserved Business slug aliases. Deactivate before transfer; independent Card activation does not enable a Disabled Business. Successful Card history is mandatory from day one and retained for Card lifetime, separately from analytics and expiring audit. Q42-Q45 settle explicit commands, idempotency keys plus expected versions, standard Admin statuses and cursor pagination. Q47 accepts atomic content-plus-revision and fresh eligibility/revision before Business/revision cache reuse, without purge-dependent publication. Strict gates trade authoritative-read cost and outage tolerance for current eligibility. Q46 defers numeric operating targets to mandatory prelaunch verification. Adapter compatibility, enforcement, provider-native retention/restore and detailed physical/API/image/cache contracts remain open gates. All four checked peer snapshots contain stale answer wording; repairs/current candidate checks remain incomplete. Draft only, no implementation or document approval. Root must append its peer-check record before freezing hashes and name the exact Draft-to-Approved status-only change.

Accepted prelaunch account review of native log/backup contents, retention, permissions, deletion/reconciliation and restore coverage for relational data and private images. Application expiry does not establish provider deletion; old restored access must be reconciled before public reopening.

Verify actual absolute/idle sessions, fresh TOTP/current membership, CSRF, identity-scoped management, grants/RLS, restricted projection, same-Business constraints and trusted-proxy/rate controls on the selected provider/runtime.

Define/test framework/adapter/HTTP/CDN ordering so fresh eligibility/revision and current-image checks precede every new delivery, including aliases, conditional responses, misses/failures and racing saves. No response cache may bypass gates.

Finish private image transformation/delivery, replacement/removal, reference commits and cleanup execution/retries. PostgreSQL/Storage are non-atomic. Unused temporary objects expire in 24 hours; post-commit cleanup failure cannot erase current references/objects or reopen old URLs.
